utterances.text: This is a new fact, Mr. Lukic. It's not just December last year. It's about 2007 that you are supposed to have become aware of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I stand by my earlier submissions, i.e., that the document does not have a title and it seems to contain an incomprehensible sort of list. Of course, if you do not see this as a justification for me to have realised the importance of this document only this late, then I am in your hands. But in view of the vagueness of this document on the face of it, the difficulty to comprehend it, you also have to keep in mind that the document did not have any sort of markings, any sort of indicators, and if the document was indeed disclosed as early as that - and I don't have reason to doubt what Mr. Saxon says - still, we were not unable [as interpreted] to grasp the importance of the document. If you think that we acted without due diligence, I suggest that you first look at the document and see all the hallmarks it bears and see how difficult it is to glean from it the actual value it might have.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, just a point of clarification. On e-court Prosecution's 65 ter number 5600, the document is described as "extract from VRS Main Staff personnel employment records." So I don't agree with Mr. Lukic's submission that it was so hard to understand at first blush what information might be in this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What I wanted to ask from Mr. Lukic is whether that it's known -- I understand that you say there is no title. But is there no narration of what the document is about in the document itself?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document contains a list --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, you're not answering my question. My question is: Is there no narration of what the document is about, a cover sheet to the document that says: This document is this, it deals with this subject? Then do you disagree with Mr. Saxon that the e-court description by the Prosecution of the document is that this is a list of personnel staff of the VRS or something like that? Surely that heading should have given an idea?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One of the Prosecution cases and one of the allegations in the indictment is that Mr. Perisic continued the practice of deploying VJ officers to the VRS and the Army of the Serbian Krajina. I think that based on such an indictment it is important for Their Honours to have the information as to when the VJ officers went to join the Army of Republika Srpska. Now, the information containing the date on their entry into duty with the VRS is something that I was unable to have until Mr. Skrbic told me about it. And this piece of information is very important for the establishment of facts in this case. Nowhere in this document is there a column with the heading "date" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, it will help us to make better progress if we can listen to one another and answer to the questions and issues that are raised. We are not now talking about the importance of this document to the case; we are talking about procedural steps that the Defence should have taken to make sure that this document can be tendered into evidence. Your learned colleague is disputing those procedural steps. Now, yes the document might be important, but if the procedural steps have not been taken it may not see the light of day within the evidence of the case no matter how important it might be. So let's listen to one another and deal with the issue at hand before we get to the next one. The point that Mr. Saxon is making is that the Prosecution gave a title to this document on the e-court when they disclosed it to the Defence in 2007. Is that when it happened, sir, the title? Don't stand up. You can take it that you can sit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, I cannot tell you at this moment when that description was placed on e-court. I can't -- I don't believe that we had our e-court system up and running in 2007. I can't make that attestment to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: All right. If you can't make, then --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But before the case began, before this trial began, we did have our documents on e-court with these descriptions, Your Honour. Certainly by September 2008 this description would have been there on e-court for P -- for Prosecution 65 ter number 5600, which contains about half the pages in this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. We now understand that we -- and we have heard Mr. Lukic's explanation. Let me ask you, Mr. Saxon, Mr. Lukic says he notified you around the 12th of April of his intention to use this document once he became aware of its significance in the trial. What prejudice, if any, does the Prosecution suffer by that late notification?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, one prejudice, Your Honour, is that the Prosecution -- it was never clear to the Prosecution where this document came from and how the Defence obtained it. And I have been trying to ascertain -- clarify that with the Defence for the last two weeks. Second of all, Your Honour, there is, as far as I'm aware, there is no English translation of this document. So the Prosecution is unable to study the specific contents of it. So with all this uncertainty, Your Honour, I submit there is prejudice to the Prosecution, for the Defence to be adding it to its 65 ter list at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for His Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: My apologies. I have very serious problems with the submissions of the parties. You know, it's becoming a cat-and-mouse game. When you now say it was never clear to the Prosecution where this document came from and how the Defence obtained it, when you have just told us that you disclosed it to the Defence and you'd -- and that Mr. Registrar tells me that the creation date of the document in e-court is the 6th of March, 2008 -- May, then I fail to understand you. You create the document, you give -- you disclose to the Defence, the Defence sends it back to you, you now query where they get it -- got it from and how the Defence obtained it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: May I interject, Your Honour, with respect?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I meant to create no confusion. I meant to imply --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, I understand your meaning. But the fact is that confusion has been created.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I accept that, Your Honour. I take your point. Your Honour, the confusion that I had was based on a number of personal discussions and e-mail conversations between myself and the Defence over the last two weeks as to why -- as to when the Defence first received this document. And it's as a result of those discussions that I finally went back and -- to our own -- to the Prosecution's own -- own disclosure records and checked when the Defence would have received a portion of this document which was in -- from -- it received a portion of this document as part of the Prosecution's 65 ter list in 2007. It received another portion during the disclosure of materials related to the testimony of this witness in late December of last year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, here's my point: My point is you created the document as far back as 2007, let us say, probably earlier than that. Okay. You disclosed it to the Defence. The Defence discloses back to you. Even if disclosing it on the 12th of April was too late for proper notice, this is a document you have had since 2007. This is a document that you have gone through and you prepared your Prosecution case. This is a document that you should therefore have gone through and be having knowledge of. What prejudice can you suffer? I mean, if we just look at the real facts, let alone the technicalities of who did what at what stage, you have had this document at least at the earliest in 2007.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The only -- the only remaining prejudice, Your Honour, is not knowing that this document was going to be part of the Defence case until this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's fine. But until the 12th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And I'm saying on the 12th of April your colleague gives you notification of his intention to use the document, a document that you have had since 2007. And the question still remains: What prejudice, if any, does the Prosecution suffer? The question of disclosure is a question of notice --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I stand --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's just notice.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I am taking your point, Your Honour, and I'm in your hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You're in my hands? You may use the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would like to give the following number to this document and that's 03332D, and I would like to call up page 1 of this document. We have it in e-court --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Am I now getting lost? I thought we are on ID 120187? Now you're coming up with a new number?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. This is the 65 ter number that I will give to it now because it's not on our list, and of course the number by which it can be found in e-court is 1D12 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: My apologies --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and we already have the English version on the screen. So 1D12-0132D -- no, the page that I want on the screen is the other one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let's take it one step at a document. The name of the document now is going to be 03332D. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And you're saying -- what page do you want?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are the corresponding pages on the screen. It's 1D12-0295, that's the B/C/S page in e-court, and the corresponding page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, what is this document about?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The copy that I'm seeing here is called the working map of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska. I also had a copy of it and I used it to monitor the situation and the activities of certain individuals in the service. It contains - and can you please zoom in the English translation. I should like to be able to see if the columns tally in the two versions. Where it says "establishment" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I just interrupt you, Mr. Skrbic, are you able to read the B/C/S on that screen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Up near the top it says the "Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska" and the same is written in the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. If you are able to read it, fine. If we could zoom in a little bit on the English side. Thank you. You may proceed. I'm sorry for the interruption.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So it says "formation" in capital letters in Serbian, that's to say "establishment." This portion of the document contains elements of the establishment of all the units, and these are elements that do not change, from the Main Staff down. The next column, if you could please zoom in on the Serbian version, although I think that's where it says "last name."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Perhaps it would be a good idea to hand a hard copy to Mr. Skrbic. I think it's fine on the screen now as well, Mr. Skrbic.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is quite visible, but I can't see the entire column so I'll use the hard copy that you've handed me now. The next column, the one next to "establishment" says "family name, first name, father's name." In that column you will see that this is the sort of information that is entered and these of course are changeable sort of elements, elements that will change. The next column says "rank." The acronym "VES" stands for military occupational speciality, and acronym "PG" stands for salary level, and actual information of course will be entered into this column as well. The next column is entitled "Pursuant to Whose Order the Appointment is Made." Data is entered into this column that will have originated from the order or the decision pursuant to which the individual has been appointed to a given post. The next column is entitled "unit/institution" with which the individual is listed, and the column contains information about the military post and the establishment rank under which the individual is listed. The next column is entitled "remarks," so that's the way it could be interpreted into English, as "remarks." And in fact what is entered into this column is the information or the date of entry into duty of that particular individual.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it possible to keep shifting so that we keep seeing these columns? Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, can you now read for us what the document states for Ratko Mladic, for General Ratko Mladic? What sort of information is indicated there?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's take it in proper order from the left to the right side. First of all, it is stated that it's the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska. That's the establishment rank. Next it says "commander." Next it says "colonel-general." Number 31099 stands for the military occupational speciality, and there is also the salary group or level which is 02. In other words, since we are with the commander it is stated that Mladic, Ratko, son of Nedjo, was appointed to this particular post whose rank at the time was lieutenant-general --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Colonel-general.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the next column it is stated that his appointment was effected pursuant to a decree of the president of Republika Srpska from 1992 in the military post 7572 at the Main Staff. His duty commenced on the 20th of May, 1992. However, in my view, Your Honour, the -- there is a mistake in the column listing his rank because his rank at the time was not one of colonel-general but one of lieutenant-general, and I can tell you that for a fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Right. Thank you so much. Did you say, sir, under the column showing "rank VES PG BOD," you said 31099 signifies the military speciality, something like that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And two columns to the right where it talks of personal rank VES, you said also VES signifies military speciality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But in this column the military speciality is signified by the figure 31180 and not 31099. What is the difference?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The difference lies in the fact that the establishment requires the VES of 31099, which means that the individual concerned has graduated from the highest-level military schools. And as for this other number, I can't really recall at this time what it stands for. But this is the actual VES of the gentleman concerned.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, and that I know what it stands for. 31 means that it's a VES of an officer. And 099 means that it -- he must have graduated from the highest-level military schools in order for him to be appointed. Now, as for 31180, I can't recall what that stands for because I do know that Mr. Mladic has graduated from the highest-level military schools and that's why he should probably have as his VES number 31099 because he had graduated from the School of National Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In order to make sure that everything is clear, let us look at your position.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see page 1D12-0310. We have a draft translation which we did in proofing. I think you will be able to follow, Your Honours. You will be able to follow the evidence of Mr. Skrbic because the information in Serbian is self-explanatory in that portion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This document doesn't give us the VES of Mr. Skrbic nor the PG of his -- nor his PG, nor his rank.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You will see the B/C/S version, Your Honours. I think that everything will become clear so that you can follow his evidence, but of course we will prepare the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And while we're waiting to see, was there -- the translation to ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Was the previous page which gave the translation about Ratko Mladic, is that official translation or draft translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That is official translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This one is draft?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think only first seven pages of the documents were official translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 20 in the electronic version, please. Could we zoom in to the middle portion, please, in the B/C/S. It's upside down.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, the Chamber does not have the entire version in English, so please tell us this portion where it says "sector for organisational, mobilisation, and personnel affairs," what does it say there?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So I'm reading from left to right. The first three columns contain permanent establishment elements which are required for this position, which means sector for organisational, mobilisation, and personnel affairs. The second column defines the name of the duty, position. Assistant commander for organisational, mobilisation, and personnel affairs. Then the next column is the establishment rank, which is major-general. Underneath we see the VES, which again indicates that this person must graduate from the School for National Defence. 05 is the PG, is the salary level. Then in the next column you see from top to bottom that this position was occupied by Stevo -- by Mico Grubor, son of Stevo, following which Petar Skrbic, son of Branko, came to this position. Could you please move to the left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: While we are at the left and you are still thinking, I have a few questions --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You didn't -- you misunderstood me. To the left on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Can we stay here in the meantime for the purposes of my question. Under the first column, sector for organisational, mobilisation, and personnel affairs, there is a figure 110, what does it mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure what that means. Perhaps it's some sort of a number which indicates which sector it is in sequence of other sectors, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you know what the figure 4500 means?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see that figure, but I don't know what it stands for, Your Honours. I can't remember all of these things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next column, there is a figure 230039. Do you know what that means?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Uh-huh -- 230039. Can I see the heading? Perhaps I can conclude based on the heading what this is about. No, I can't make any conclusions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Then you can ask the screen to go where you wanted it to go. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Thank you. Now, Your Honours, I know what this is about so I can give you very specific information. At the time when I was appointed, my rank was that of a colonel, not major-general. My real VES is 31378, which means that I have graduated from the school for anti-aircraft defence, rocket department. And then this other number means that I graduated from the -- another military school after the military academy. The next column indicates that I was appointed by means of a decree of the president of Republika Srpska, number 01-1585/94. The next column says that I serve at the military post 7572, which stands for the Main Staff of the VRS, that's its military post number. And then the next column indicates that I was appointed on the 15th of August, 1994, that's the date of entry into service for that position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm struggling to find these numbers 01-1585/94. I can see 7572. So I'm not quite sure where you were when you were talking about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the number of the presidential decree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I've got it. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, there's a discrepancy that I have just seen, and it pertains both to Mr. Mladic's data and your data. In both situations you observed that the factual situation concerning the rank did not correspond to what the rank was at the time of the appointment. My question is: Was it possible that this information was entered later? Because it says here that you were major-general and the same applied to Mladic, and you said in relation to both of you that at the time of the appointment neither of you had the rank indicated here. So do you know about this without speculating?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not speculating. I'm not speculating, Mr. Lukic. The data processing people who receive this information, they get a whole bunch of documents and there is a delay in entering. And when they know the actual rank, then they enter the actual rank. So there is a discrepancy here between the actual rank and the rank indicated here. As for other columns, they reflect actual data. The data processing clerk simply knew, knew the ranks that we held in real time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. So who enters data into this database?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The data is entered by computer specialists based on the documents that are given to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Another question. During our proofing session we went over this document and you explained it to me. Do you know in this column where it says on the basis of whose order the appointment was made, in relation to the entire document whose orders were these, of which authorities, of which state? So which state issued the orders appointing all of these persons and in which army was it done?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of these orders or decrees - and sometimes there were orders issued and sometimes decrees - it is the president that issues decrees and all other commanders issue orders. So all of this data is entered exclusively on the basis of enactments of the Army of Republika Srpska and the state of Republika Srpska when it comes to decrees because, as I said, the decrees are issued by the president of the country.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we tender this into evidence and MFI it. And I don't want to burden either the CLSS or you, and I propose that I get in touch with CLSS to see what exactly needs to be translated and I can co-ordinate this with Mr. Saxon to see that only the bits that are important for this case are translated. But so as not to waste any further time, I suggest that we mark this document for identification as Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do have an objection to make, not to the document per say, to the fact that I note at page 61, line 20, Mr. Lukic begins his question saying: "During our proofing session we went over this document and you explained it to me." I certainly would like to state for the record that I don't believe in any proofing note we have received any explanation of this document from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, this is a completely different issue. What bearing does it have on the tendering of this document into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm not objecting to the tendering of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sure. So can we deal with the tendering of the evidence --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- of this document. And then you can raise your problems with Mr. Lukic separately. The document then is admitted into evidence and marked for identification. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be Exhibit D330, marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Saxon, do you want to pitch a fight with Mr. Lukic about what he should and shouldn't have done during proofing or after proofing?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm searching in the Rules for an appropriate Rule to cite and I'm not finding -- I'm not finding it. I will raise this matter at a later time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If I can find better grounds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, for the sake of the transcript I have to comment on what Mr. Saxon has just said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before you --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and it has to do --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before you do that, can we just have it on record that this document is MFI'd for further translations. Thank you. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Wishing to avoid any problems with translation of the document, in my meeting with Mr. Saxon and Mr. Harmon a week ago, I suggested to Mr. Saxon concerning this column where it says pursuant to whose orders the appointment was made, meaning that it was done only on the basis of enactments of the Army of Republika Srpska, I indicated to Mr. Saxon a week ago what I had heard from Mr. Skrbic, and I mentioned it to him wishing to avoid burdening the CLSS any further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What are you addressing?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But that was my intention but I will need to do it now. Mr. Saxon has just said that he didn't know that in my proofing I went over this with Mr. Skrbic, and this is why he's now against us tendering this document into evidence. And what I'm claiming is that Mr. Saxon was aware of the fact and that he was informed so during the meeting we had with him and Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, in the interests of time, let's again listen to one another. Mr. Saxon has withdrawn this objection pending him finding the relevant Rule that supports him in the Rules. So you will respond to him at that time, not now. Okay. Thank you. Carry on with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are forgiven.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now move to a different topic. Just a second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Mr. Skrbic, what were the competencies of your sector? We're now moving to a completely different topic, to status issues within the service, and I would like to go -- to refer to the legal regulations. What are the competencies of your sector when it comes to appointing certain persons to positions in the Army of Republika Srpska? What do you do? What kind of information do you receive? And what do you decide upon and how do you decide upon it?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The sector that I headed dealt with personnel, organisational, and mobilisational issues. I do not want to tire down anyone listening to me, so I will only speak about the main part of the work conducted by my sector which were the personnel affairs. And this part of our work contains the schooling, proposals for promotion, proposals for transfer, and proposals for deployment and appointments of active and reserve officers of the Army of Republika Srpska, based on the proposal of data that we received from subordinate units which were corps commands.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Let us go subject by subject. Let us first deal with appointments, appointments to positions. What do you do? Who makes the proposal? What is then done? And who makes the final decision?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Appointments, promotions, and transfers were done almost simultaneously. However, since you asked me about appointments, then this is what I can say. We prepare documents and proposals for the commander of the Main Staff on appointments of certain position -- certain persons to certain establishment positions, and we saw that this was all defined in establishment terms. These appointment proposals are debated at the collegium of the Main Staff, where all members of the Main Staff can participate in the discussion. However, it is the commander of the Main Staff that makes the final decision and informs everybody of it. For example, Petar Petrovic will be appointed brigade commander. Following that, we write up the order on appointment if it involves a rank up to the level of colonel. When it comes to generals or colonels promoted to establishment positions of a general, then we prepare paperwork, take it to the president of the republic, a commander of the Main Staff gives the explanation. If the president adopts that explanation, then he issues a presidential decree; if not, then that appointment is denied. When I said "president of the republic," I was referring to president of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In that decision-making on appointments, did anybody from the Army of Yugoslavia participate in that process?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody from the Army of Yugoslavia influenced this process at any stage, either directly or indirectly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did this process have anything to do with the 30th Personnel Centre; and if so, what was it when it came to appointments?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only link that existed was that a new, amended information was provided by the Army of Republika Srpska to the 30th Personnel Centre in order for that new information to be entered into records and in order to regulate the entitlements that that person has based on that position in terms of salary level, et cetera, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us take you as an example. You were assistant commander for morale in the 2nd Krajina Corps, and then in August of 1994 you were appointed assistant commander at the Main Staff. The change of the establishment position, did it also entail a change in the salary level, in the quotient based on which salary was calculated?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can give you a very specific answer, because in the 2nd Krajina Corps my salary level was 07. Once I transferred to the Main Staff, even though I still had the same rank of colonel, my salary level was 05, even though it's a lower number it actually means that I was entitled to bigger benefits.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have 65 ter of Defence 00231D, could we call that document up, please. While we're waiting for the English, this is a decree, a decree of the president of the republic, of Republika Srpska, dated the 15th of June, 1992, by way of which Bogdan Subotic is appointed to the Government of Republika Srpska, according -- he's appointed minister of defence according to the peace time and war time establishment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber has already seen a number of such documents, so I will not dwell on this, but when we spoke about competencies earlier on, tell us who was competent for deciding to appoint persons to this establishment position?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the president of Republika Srpska who has the power to do that. Now, as to who proposed this person to this position, I don't know that. Given that the minister of defence is a civilian organ, then Mr. Subotic could not become employed there since he was in the military. So in the Army of Republika Srpska the personnel of the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry, Mr. Skrbic, the interpreter missed something she would like you to repeat. She's been with you up to where you said "given that the minister of defence is a civilian organ, then Mr. Subotic could not become employed there since he was in the military." Can you then continue from there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have to specify. He could become employed at the Ministry of Defence, which is a civilian organ, but he could not become employed as a civilian because he was in the military. I hope the interpreter is following me well. Up until that time in the army -- or rather, due to that time -- due to that, in the Army of Republika Srpska there was a special department filled by military persons. And whenever the Ministry of Defence had people employed there who were in the military, they had to be appointed pursuant to establishment terms. As a result of that, this decree is in accordance with that principle even though General Subotic was appointed to the Ministry of Defence which was a civilian organ. I hope I was clear enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is the interpreters who had asked you to repeat yourself. I hope you have been clear enough to them. I don't ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the witness was rather clear. Now, to what extent all of us understand this is a different matter. These are very, very narrow, professional, specialised concepts. So, Your Honours, can we tender this into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. I wasn't sure whether you were saying: No, I object, or whether -- okay. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D331. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now could we please see the Defence Exhibit D118. We will have to go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into closed session -- do you want closed session or do you want private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, private, private, Your Honour. Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Skrbic, I remind you once again of what I told you at the end of the session yesterday, not to talk to anybody about the case until and unless you are excused from further testifying. We stand adjourned to tomorrow at, again, 9.00 in the morning, the same courtroom. We hope we will not have the technical problems that we had this morning and that we will start promptly at 9.00 tomorrow. And have a good rest. Court adjourned.
